title: Reciprocal and demonstrative reference
explanation: 彼此 refers to the two parties mutually or to both of them; 如此 means so or in this way and refers back to an already known situation.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该彼此尊重。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi bǐcǐ zūnzhòng.
examples.translation: We should respect each other.

examples.hanzi: 事情并非如此简单。
examples.pinyin: Shìqing bìngfēi rúcǐ jiǎndān.
examples.translation: The matter is not that simple.

title: Specific classifiers
pattern: number + 册／朵／幅／届／颗／匹／扇 + noun
explanation: 册 counts volumes, 朵 flowers and clouds, 幅 pictures and paintings, 届 editions of events or graduating classes. 颗 counts small round objects, 匹 horses and lengths of cloth, 扇 doors and windows.

examples.hanzi: 她买了一册书和两幅画。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yī cè shū hé liǎng fú huà.
examples.translation: She bought one volume and two paintings.

examples.hanzi: 一匹马站在那扇门旁边。
examples.pinyin: Yī pǐ mǎ zhàn zài nà shàn mén pángbiān.
examples.translation: A horse is standing beside that door.

examples.hanzi: 这届学生种了花，现在开了三朵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiè xuésheng zhòng le huā, xiànzài kāi le sān duǒ.
examples.translation: The students in this year group planted flowers, and three have now bloomed.

examples.hanzi: 夜空中只有一颗星星。
examples.pinyin: Yèkōng zhōng zhǐ yǒu yī kē xīngxing.
examples.translation: There is only one star in the night sky.

title: Degree and special emphasis
pattern: 过于／可／稍／稍微／尤其 + predicate
explanation: 过于 indicates an excessive degree; 稍 and 稍微 soften the degree, often with 一点儿. 可 strengthens an evaluation in speech, while 尤其 singles out one case in comparison with others.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法过于复杂。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ guòyú fùzá.
examples.translation: This method is too complicated.

examples.hanzi: 请稍微等一下。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng shāowēi děng yīxià.
examples.translation: Please wait a little while.

examples.hanzi: 这条路可远了，晚上尤其难走。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù kě yuǎn le, wǎnshang yóuqí nán zǒu.
examples.translation: This road is really long and is especially difficult to travel along at night.

title: The majority
explanation: 大都 presents what applies to most members of a set, allowing for exceptions. It comes before the predicate and does not require an additional 都.

examples.hanzi: 这里的居民大都会说普通话。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de jūmín dàdōu huì shuō pǔtōnghuà.
examples.translation: Most residents here can speak Mandarin.

examples.hanzi: 这些书我大都看过。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū wǒ dàdōu kàn guo.
examples.translation: I have read nearly all these books.

title: Time, continuity, and habit
pattern: 不时／将／将要／仍旧／时常／时刻／依旧／一向 + predicate
explanation: 将 and 将要 announce a future event, with 将 being more formal; 仍旧 and 依旧 indicate that a situation continues unchanged. 不时 means from time to time, 时常 often, 时刻 at every moment, and 一向 always or habitually.

examples.hanzi: 会议明天将开始。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì míngtiān jiāng kāishǐ.
examples.translation: The meeting will begin tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 他依旧住在这里，不时来看我。
examples.pinyin: Tā yījiù zhù zài zhèlǐ, bùshí lái kàn wǒ.
examples.translation: He still lives here and comes to visit me from time to time.

examples.hanzi: 她一向认真，时刻注意安全。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīxiàng rènzhēn, shíkè zhùyì ānquán.
examples.translation: She has always been conscientious and pays constant attention to safety.

title: Occasionally and again
explanation: 偶尔 indicates a low, irregular frequency; 再次 indicates another occurrence of an event that has already happened, often in a formal register.

examples.hanzi: 我偶尔在外面吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ ǒu'ěr zài wàimian chīfàn.
examples.translation: I occasionally eat out.

examples.hanzi: 老师再次解释了这个词。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zàicì jiěshì le zhège cí.
examples.translation: The teacher explained this word again.

title: In secret
explanation: 偷偷 describes an action performed without being noticed or informing others. 地 is optional.

examples.hanzi: 孩子偷偷打开了盒子。
examples.pinyin: Háizi tōutōu dǎkāi le hézi.
examples.translation: The child secretly opened the box.

examples.hanzi: 她偷偷地给妈妈准备了礼物。
examples.pinyin: Tā tōutōu de gěi māma zhǔnbèi le lǐwù.
examples.translation: She secretly prepared a present for her mother.

title: Adverbs expressing attitude
pattern: 毕竟／不免／差点儿／倒是／干脆／就／居然／可／明明／总算
explanation: 毕竟 recalls a fact to take into account, 不免 a reaction that is hard to avoid, and 差点儿 an event that nearly happened. 倒是 introduces a contrast, 干脆 a decisive choice, and 就 firm insistence; 居然 expresses surprise and 可 strengthens the tone. 明明 emphasizes an obvious fact, often contradicted by something else, and 总算 an achievement finally attained.

examples.hanzi: 他毕竟是新来的，不免有些紧张。
examples.pinyin: Tā bìjìng shì xīn lái de, bùmiǎn yǒuxiē jǐnzhāng.
examples.translation: After all, he has only just arrived, so it is inevitable that he feels a little nervous.

examples.hanzi: 我差点儿摔倒，你倒是笑了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chàdiǎnr shuāidǎo, nǐ dàoshi xiào le.
examples.translation: I almost fell over, but you just started laughing.

examples.hanzi: 既然没车了，我们干脆走回去。
examples.pinyin: Jìrán méi chē le, wǒmen gāncuì zǒu huíqù.
examples.translation: Since there is no transport left, let us simply walk back.

examples.hanzi: 我就不去，你可别生气。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiù bù qù, nǐ kě bié shēngqì.
examples.translation: I am definitely not going, but please do not get angry.

examples.hanzi: 他明明没学过，居然全答对了。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngmíng méi xué guo, jūrán quán dá duì le.
examples.translation: He clearly had never studied it, yet he got every answer right.

examples.hanzi: 等了半天，车总算来了。
examples.pinyin: Děng le bàntiān, chē zǒngsuàn lái le.
examples.translation: After a long wait, the bus finally arrived.

title: As a situation changes
explanation: 随着 introduces a process or change accompanying the development described in the main clause. It does not simply mean after a completed event.

examples.hanzi: 随着天气变暖，花都开了。
examples.pinyin: Suízhe tiānqì biàn nuǎn, huā dōu kāi le.
examples.translation: As the weather warmed up, all the flowers bloomed.

examples.hanzi: 随着经验的增加，他更自信了。
examples.pinyin: Suízhe jīngyàn de zēngjiā, tā gèng zìxìn le.
examples.translation: As his experience grew, he became more confident.

title: 将 as an object marker
explanation: 将 introduces the object being acted upon, like 把, especially in writing and formal instructions. The predicate normally specifies a result, destination, or other outcome of the action; here 将 is not the future adverb.

examples.hanzi: 请将姓名写在纸上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiāng xìngmíng xiě zài zhǐ shang.
examples.translation: Please write your name on the paper.

examples.hanzi: 他将旧书送给了学校。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiāng jiù shū sòng gěi le xuéxiào.
examples.translation: He donated the old books to the school.

title: Introducing the responsible party with 由
explanation: 由 introduces the person who performs or takes responsibility for a task. The matter to be handled can be placed first as the topic; this does not necessarily imply a passive construction describing a negative event.

examples.hanzi: 这次会议由我主持。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huìyì yóu wǒ zhǔchí.
examples.translation: I will chair this meeting.

examples.hanzi: 费用由公司承担。
examples.pinyin: Fèiyòng yóu gōngsī chéngdān.
examples.translation: The company covers the expenses.

title: Means or entitlement: 凭
explanation: 凭 introduces what an action relies on: ability, evidence, documents, or other means. It can also indicate the entitlement that gives access to something.

examples.hanzi: 凭这张票可以进去。
examples.pinyin: Píng zhè zhāng piào kěyǐ jìnqù.
examples.translation: You can enter with this ticket.

examples.hanzi: 不能只凭感觉做决定。
examples.pinyin: Bù néng zhǐ píng gǎnjué zuò juédìng.
examples.translation: You cannot make decisions based on feelings alone.

title: The basis for an evaluation
explanation: 依据 introduces the facts, data, or criteria underpinning a conclusion or decision. It is typical of formal language and highlights the basis of the reasoning.

examples.hanzi: 我们依据事实作出判断。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yījù shìshí zuòchū pànduàn.
examples.translation: We make judgments based on facts.

examples.hanzi: 依据调查结果，计划需要调整。
examples.pinyin: Yījù diàochá jiéguǒ, jìhuà xūyào tiáozhěng.
examples.translation: Based on the survey results, the plan needs to be revised.

title: Compliance with a rule
explanation: 依照 introduces a rule, instruction, or model followed when carrying out an action. Rather than simply providing an informational basis, it emphasizes compliance.

examples.hanzi: 请依照说明操作。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yīzhào shuōmíng cāozuò.
examples.translation: Please follow the instructions.

examples.hanzi: 我们依照规定办理手续。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīzhào guīdìng bànlǐ shǒuxù.
examples.translation: We handle the procedures according to the regulations.

title: Linking consequences, additions, and sequences
explanation: 从而 links a result to the preceding situation; 加上 adds a factor contributing to the outcome. 完了 colloquially introduces what comes next, while 一旦 introduces a condition that triggers a consequence once fulfilled.

examples.hanzi: 他改进了方法，从而提高了效率。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǎijìn le fāngfǎ, cóng'ér tígāo le xiàolǜ.
examples.translation: He improved the method, thereby increasing efficiency.

examples.hanzi: 路远，加上下雨，我们迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Lù yuǎn, jiāshàng xià yǔ, wǒmen chídào le.
examples.translation: The journey was long, and it was raining as well, so we arrived late.

examples.hanzi: 先洗菜，完了再切。
examples.pinyin: Xiān xǐ cài, wán le zài qiē.
examples.translation: Wash the vegetables first, then cut them.

examples.hanzi: 一旦发现问题，请马上报告。
examples.pinyin: Yīdàn fāxiàn wèntí, qǐng mǎshàng bàogào.
examples.translation: As soon as you discover a problem, report it immediately.

title: Alternatives with 也好
explanation: 也好 can present alternatives considered equally acceptable; the conclusion applies to all of them. After a suggestion, it can also express acceptance, meaning that is fine too.

examples.hanzi: 坐车也好，走路也好，我都可以。
examples.pinyin: Zuò chē yě hǎo, zǒu lù yě hǎo, wǒ dōu kěyǐ.
examples.translation: Taking transport or walking is fine with me.

examples.hanzi: 你先回家也好，路上还要走一个小时呢。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān huí jiā yě hǎo, lù shang hái yào zǒu yī ge xiǎoshí ne.
examples.translation: Going home early is fine too: you still have an hour to walk.

title: Repeated actions with 来 and 去
explanation: Repeating the same verb with 来 and 去 describes a repeated action or repeated consideration of possibilities. It does not necessarily indicate physical movement.

examples.hanzi: 我想来想去，还是决定留下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng lái xiǎng qù, háishi juédìng liúxià.
examples.translation: After thinking it over and over, I still decided to stay.

examples.hanzi: 他在门口走来走去。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài ménkǒu zǒu lái zǒu qù.
examples.translation: He walks back and forth in front of the door.

title: A change during an action
pattern: verb + 着 + verb + 着，就 + event
explanation: Repetition with 着 presents an ongoing activity during which another event, often unexpected, occurs. It does not simply indicate two actions continuing together.

examples.hanzi: 我们谈着谈着，就忘了时间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tán zhe tán zhe, jiù wàng le shíjiān.
examples.translation: We lost track of time while talking.

examples.hanzi: 孩子走着走着，突然停了下来。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zǒu zhe zǒu zhe, tūrán tíng le xiàlái.
examples.translation: The child suddenly stopped while walking.

title: Paired absence with 没
explanation: This structure combines two associated elements to describe an overall lack, often in a colloquial, critical tone. The combinations are conventional, such as 没日没夜 or 没大没小, rather than freely formed.

examples.hanzi: 他没日没夜地照顾病人。
examples.pinyin: Tā méi rì méi yè de zhàogù bìngrén.
examples.translation: He cares for the sick day and night without stopping.

examples.hanzi: 别跟长辈没大没小的。
examples.pinyin: Bié gēn zhǎngbèi méi dà méi xiǎo de.
examples.translation: Do not treat your elders disrespectfully.

title: From decision to action
explanation: By repeating the verb, 说A就A expresses an immediate shift from decision to action. It can praise readiness or criticize a sudden action.

examples.hanzi: 他拿起包，说走就走。
examples.pinyin: Tā ná qǐ bāo, shuō zǒu jiù zǒu.
examples.translation: He picked up his bag and left on the spot.

examples.hanzi: 这孩子说哭就哭。
examples.pinyin: Zhè háizi shuō kū jiù kū.
examples.translation: This child starts crying at the drop of a hat.

title: Two associated qualities or features
explanation: 有A有B brings together two aspects present at the same time, often in conventional expressions such as 有说有笑. With nouns, it can list complementary features of a place or group.

examples.hanzi: 大家有说有笑地回家了。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yǒu shuō yǒu xiào de huí jiā le.
examples.translation: Everyone went home chatting and laughing.

examples.hanzi: 这个村子有山有水。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cūnzi yǒu shān yǒu shuǐ.
examples.translation: This village has mountains and streams.

title: Extraordinary or alarming: 不得了
explanation: 不得了 can be an exclamation of admiration or signal a serious situation. After 得, it strongly intensifies an adjective or emotional state.

examples.hanzi: 她能说五种语言，真不得了。
examples.pinyin: Tā néng shuō wǔ zhǒng yǔyán, zhēn bùdéliǎo.
examples.translation: She can speak five languages; she is truly remarkable.

examples.hanzi: 不得了，厨房冒烟了。
examples.pinyin: Bùdéliǎo, chúfáng mào yān le.
examples.translation: Help! Smoke is coming out of the kitchen.

title: Modestly declining praise
explanation: 不敢当 is a polite response to praise, honors, or thanks felt to be excessive. It expresses modesty, not a practical inability to do something.

examples.hanzi: 您说得太好了，我实在不敢当。
examples.pinyin: Nín shuō de tài hǎo le, wǒ shízài bù gǎn dāng.
examples.translation: You flatter me; I really do not deserve such praise.

examples.hanzi: 不敢当，我只是帮了一点儿忙。
examples.pinyin: Bù gǎn dāng, wǒ zhǐshì bāng le yīdiǎnr máng.
examples.translation: I do not deserve so much credit; I only helped a little.

title: Settling a matter with 得了
explanation: 得了 after a suggestion means simply to do that and settle the matter. 得了吧 instead tells someone to stop or rejects a statement with disbelief; here it is pronounced dé le.

examples.hanzi: 太晚了，明天再去得了。
examples.pinyin: Tài wǎn le, míngtiān zài qù dé le.
examples.translation: It is too late; let us just go tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 得了吧，我才不信呢。
examples.pinyin: Dé le ba, wǒ cái bù xìn ne.
examples.translation: Oh, stop it. I do not believe that at all.

title: There is no need
explanation: 用不着 denies the necessity of an action, not its possibility. It can reassure someone or firmly reject unsolicited intervention.

examples.hanzi: 用不着买票，今天免费。
examples.pinyin: Yòngbuzháo mǎi piào, jīntiān miǎnfèi.
examples.translation: There is no need to buy a ticket; it is free today.

examples.hanzi: 你用不着为我担心。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yòngbuzháo wèi wǒ dānxīn.
examples.translation: You do not need to worry about me.

title: Evaluating from a clue
explanation: 从……来看 introduces the perspective or data from which an evaluation is derived. It does not necessarily present someone’s personal opinion.

examples.hanzi: 从结果来看，这个办法有效。
examples.pinyin: Cóng jiéguǒ lái kàn, zhège bànfǎ yǒuxiào.
examples.translation: Judging by the results, this method works.

examples.hanzi: 从长远来看，学习很值得。
examples.pinyin: Cóng chángyuǎn lái kàn, xuéxí hěn zhíde.
examples.translation: In the long run, studying is really worthwhile.

title: Up to a limit
explanation: 到……为止 sets a time limit or a point beyond which something does not continue. With 目前, it means up to now, without claiming that the future situation will remain identical.

examples.hanzi: 到目前为止，还没有人报名。
examples.pinyin: Dào mùqián wéizhǐ, hái méiyǒu rén bàomíng.
examples.translation: So far, nobody has signed up.

examples.hanzi: 今天的讨论到这里为止。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tǎolùn dào zhèlǐ wéizhǐ.
examples.translation: Today’s discussion ends here.

title: A considerable degree with 够
pattern: 够 + adjective + 的；够 + person + verb + 的
explanation: 够……的 colloquially evaluates a degree as considerable, sometimes with surprise or criticism. With a person before the predicate, it can indicate that something is enough to keep them busy or cause them difficulty.

examples.hanzi: 这道题够难的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào tí gòu nán de.
examples.translation: This exercise is really difficult.

examples.hanzi: 这些工作够他忙的。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē gōngzuò gòu tā máng de.
examples.translation: This job is enough to keep him very busy.

title: Taking a case as an example
explanation: 拿……来说 introduces a specific case chosen to illustrate a more general statement. It does not describe physically taking something.

examples.hanzi: 拿交通来说，这里很方便。
examples.pinyin: Ná jiāotōng lái shuō, zhèlǐ hěn fāngbiàn.
examples.translation: Take transport, for example: it is very convenient here.

examples.hanzi: 拿我弟弟来说，他每天都跑步。
examples.pinyin: Ná wǒ dìdi lái shuō, tā měitiān dōu pǎobù.
examples.translation: Take my younger brother: he runs every day.

title: Distributing contrasting characteristics
explanation: This pattern divides a set into groups with different, often opposite properties: some are A, others B. It can highlight inconsistency or an unsuitable situation.

examples.hanzi: 这些鞋大的大，小的小。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē xié dà de dà, xiǎo de xiǎo.
examples.translation: Some of these shoes are too big, and others are too small.

examples.hanzi: 院子里的树高的高，矮的矮。
examples.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ de shù gāo de gāo, ǎi de ǎi.
examples.translation: There are tall trees and short trees in the courtyard.

title: From someone’s point of view
explanation: 在……看来 explicitly attributes an evaluation to a person or group. It distinguishes that perspective from a statement presented as universal.

examples.hanzi: 在我看来，健康最重要。
examples.pinyin: Zài wǒ kànlái, jiànkāng zuì zhòngyào.
examples.translation: In my view, health is the most important thing.

examples.hanzi: 在孩子们看来，这只是个游戏。
examples.pinyin: Zài háizimen kànlái, zhè zhǐshì ge yóuxì.
examples.translation: In the children’s eyes, it is only a game.

title: The semantic role of the object
explanation: An element after the verb can semantically be the agent, such as the person arriving in a presentational sentence, despite occupying the object position. A patient object instead indicates what receives the action; syntactic position alone does not determine semantic role.

examples.hanzi: 门外来了一位医生。
examples.pinyin: Mén wài lái le yī wèi yīshēng.
examples.translation: A doctor arrived outside the door.

examples.hanzi: 医生检查了孩子的眼睛。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le háizi de yǎnjing.
examples.translation: The doctor examined the child’s eyes.

title: Multiple elements before the verb
explanation: Several modifiers can precede the same verb: time and place expressions tend to come before manner expressions closer to the verb. Purpose, perspective, and communicative emphasis can alter the order; it is not an invariant mechanical sequence.

examples.hanzi: 他昨天在办公室认真地检查了报告。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuótiān zài bàngōngshì rènzhēn de jiǎnchá le bàogào.
examples.translation: Yesterday in the office, he checked the report carefully.

examples.hanzi: 为了考试，她每天在家复习到很晚。
examples.pinyin: Wèile kǎoshì, tā měitiān zài jiā fùxí dào hěn wǎn.
examples.translation: To prepare for the exam, she studies at home until late every day.

title: Beginning and continuation with directional complements
pattern: verb + 上／起来；verb + 下去／下来
explanation: 上 and 起来 can indicate the beginning of an activity without spatial movement. 下去 projects continuation into the future, while 下来 can present continuity maintained up to the reference point.

examples.hanzi: 他们一见面就谈上了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yī jiànmiàn jiù tán shàng le.
examples.translation: As soon as they met, they started talking.

examples.hanzi: 听到这个消息，她笑了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā xiào le qǐlái.
examples.translation: On hearing the news, she started laughing.

examples.hanzi: 请继续说下去。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jìxù shuō xiàqù.
examples.translation: Please go on speaking.

examples.hanzi: 这个习惯我一直保持下来了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xíguàn wǒ yīzhí bǎochí xiàlái le.
examples.translation: I have maintained this habit to this day.

title: Possibility or permissibility with 得 and 不得
explanation: After certain verbs, 得 and 不得 express whether an action is possible, tolerable, or permitted. The negative form can mean must not, not just cannot manage to; here 得 is pronounced de.

examples.hanzi: 这种水果吃得吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ chī de ma?
examples.translation: Can this kind of fruit be eaten?

examples.hanzi: 这件东西碰不得。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn dōngxi pèng bu de.
examples.translation: This object must not be touched.

title: Extreme degree and emotional effects
pattern: predicate + 得 + 不得了／慌／厉害；predicate + 坏／透 + 了
explanation: 得不得了, 得慌, and 得厉害 indicate an intense degree; 慌 occurs mainly with unpleasant feelings such as suffocation or boredom. 坏了 and 透了 can intensify emotions or states, beyond their literal meanings of damage and penetration.

examples.hanzi: 孩子高兴得不得了。
examples.pinyin: Háizi gāoxìng de bùdéliǎo.
examples.translation: The child is extremely happy.

examples.hanzi: 我饿得慌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ è de huang.
examples.translation: I am terribly hungry.

examples.hanzi: 我的头疼得厉害。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóu téng de lìhai.
examples.translation: My head hurts a lot.

examples.hanzi: 你一直不回来，可把我急坏了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīzhí bù huílái, kě bǎ wǒ jí huài le.
examples.translation: You took so long to return that I was worried sick.

examples.hanzi: 他对这个结果失望透了。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège jiéguǒ shīwàng tòu le.
examples.translation: He is deeply disappointed with this result.

title: A state described by a whole expression
explanation: After 得, a state or effect can be described by a verb phrase, a clause with its own subject, or a fixed expression. The complement makes the manner or degree of the preceding predicate concrete.

examples.hanzi: 她累得不想说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā lèi de bù xiǎng shuōhuà.
examples.translation: She is so tired that she does not feel like talking.

examples.hanzi: 我紧张得手都出汗了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jǐnzhāng de shǒu dōu chū hàn le.
examples.translation: I was so nervous that even my palms were sweating.

examples.hanzi: 他急得走来走去。
examples.pinyin: Tā jí de zǒu lái zǒu qù.
examples.translation: He was so agitated that he kept pacing back and forth.

title: Persistent existence and inscriptions with 有
pattern: subject + 有着 + object；surface + verb + 有 + content
explanation: 有着 presents the existence or possession of a relatively stable characteristic, relationship, or state. After verbs such as 写 or 刻, 有 signals that some content is present on a surface.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市有着丰富的文化。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu zhe fēngfù de wénhuà.
examples.translation: This city has a rich culture.

examples.hanzi: 墙上写有安全提示。
examples.pinyin: Qiáng shang xiě yǒu ānquán tíshì.
examples.translation: Safety warnings are written on the wall.

title: Four extensions of 把 sentences
pattern: 把 + object + adverbial／一 + verb／verb了／verb + object
explanation: The object introduced by 把 is handled or changed: an adverbial can specify how or where the action takes place. 一 followed by the verb presents a quick gesture opening a sequence; 了 can complete the predicate when context clarifies the outcome. A second object can express the use, destination, or result of the initial object.

examples.hanzi: 别把衣服到处乱放。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ yīfu dàochù luàn fàng.
examples.translation: Do not leave clothes scattered messily everywhere.

examples.hanzi: 他把书一合，就站了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shū yī hé, jiù zhàn le qǐlái.
examples.translation: He closed the book in one motion and stood up.

examples.hanzi: 我把那件事忘了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ nà jiàn shì wàng le.
examples.translation: I forgot about that matter.

examples.hanzi: 她把存款买了车。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ cúnkuǎn mǎi le chē.
examples.translation: He used his savings to buy a car.

title: Passive meaning without a marker
explanation: In a notional passive, the initial element undergoes the action, but 被 is absent. Context and the result show that it is not the agent; the person performing the action can remain unexpressed.

examples.hanzi: 房间已经打扫干净了。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān yǐjīng dǎsǎo gānjìng le.
examples.translation: The room has already been cleaned.

examples.hanzi: 自行车修好了。
examples.pinyin: Zìxíngchē xiū hǎo le.
examples.translation: The bicycle has been repaired.

title: Logical relationships between serial predicates
pattern: same subject + predicate A + predicate B
explanation: Two predicates referring to the same subject can be linked without an explicit conjunction. The second can be a consequence of the first, contrast with it, or express what becomes possible because of it; context clarifies the relationship.

examples.hanzi: 他生病住院了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēng bìng zhù yuàn le.
examples.translation: He became ill and was admitted to hospital.

examples.hanzi: 这本书我买了没看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ mǎi le méi kàn.
examples.translation: I bought this book but have not read it.

examples.hanzi: 她有时间帮你。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu shíjiān bāng nǐ.
examples.translation: He has time to help you.

title: Causing a reaction with 叫、令、使、让
pattern: cause + 叫／令／使／让 + person + predicate
explanation: The person after the causative verb is both its object and the subject of the following predicate. These verbs can describe an emotional or practical effect, not just an order: 令 and 使 are more formal, while 叫 and 让 are more common in speech.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息让我们很高兴。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi ràng wǒmen hěn gāoxìng.
examples.translation: This news makes us very happy.

examples.hanzi: 他的回答令我吃惊。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huídá lìng wǒ chījīng.
examples.translation: His answer surprised me.

examples.hanzi: 这场病使他瘦了很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bìng shǐ tā shòu le hěn duō.
examples.translation: This illness has made him lose a lot of weight.

examples.hanzi: 这件事叫她很为难。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì jiào tā hěn wéinán.
examples.translation: This situation puts her in a very difficult position.

title: Explicit comparison and measured difference
pattern: 跟 + comparison term + 相比；A + adjective + B + quantity
explanation: 跟……相比 establishes the reference point for evaluating a situation. With adjectives expressing a measurable difference, such as 大、高 or 早, the second term can directly follow the adjective before the quantity, without 比.

examples.hanzi: 跟去年相比，今年雨水更多。
examples.pinyin: Gēn qùnián xiāngbǐ, jīnnián yǔshuǐ gèng duō.
examples.translation: Compared with last year, there is more rain this year.

examples.hanzi: 姐姐大我三岁。
examples.pinyin: Jiějie dà wǒ sān suì.
examples.translation: My older sister is three years older than me.

title: Declarative alternatives
explanation: 或是……或是…… presents alternative possibilities in a statement. It is not the usual interrogative choice with 还是 and does not imply that one alternative has already been decided on.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们或是爬山，或是在家休息。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen huòshì pá shān, huòshì zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.translation: At the weekend, we will either go to the mountains or rest at home.

examples.hanzi: 你可以或是打电话，或是发邮件。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ huòshì dǎ diànhuà, huòshì fā yóujiàn.
examples.translation: You can call or send an email.

title: Concession involving a real fact
pattern: 尽管 + fact，但是／可是 + contrast
explanation: 尽管 acknowledges an actual fact that would lead one to expect a different outcome; 但是 or 可是 introduces the unexpected outcome. It differs from 即使, which can concede a merely hypothetical condition.

examples.hanzi: 尽管下着雨，但是比赛没有取消。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn xià zhe yǔ, dànshì bǐsài méiyǒu qǔxiāo.
examples.translation: Although it was raining, the competition was not canceled.

examples.hanzi: 尽管很累，可是她还在工作。
examples.pinyin: Jǐnguǎn hěn lèi, kěshì tā hái zài gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Although she is very tired, she is still working.

title: When an event occurs
explanation: 一旦 presents a condition whose fulfillment triggers a result, often with particular significance or difficulty of reversal. It does not indicate a habit repeated each time, as 每次 does.

examples.hanzi: 一旦答应了，就要做到。
examples.pinyin: Yīdàn dāying le, jiù yào zuòdào.
examples.translation: Once you make a promise, you must keep it.

examples.hanzi: 一旦发现着火，就要立即报警。
examples.pinyin: Yīdàn fāxiàn zháohuǒ, jiù yào lìjí bàojǐng.
examples.translation: As soon as you notice a fire, you must raise the alarm immediately.

title: A condition and a negative alternative
pattern: 要是 + condition，（就）+ outcome，否则 + alternative
explanation: 要是 introduces a hypothetical condition, and 就 can mark its consequence. 否则 presents what would happen without that condition; the reference must remain clear.

examples.hanzi: 要是你有空，就来帮忙，否则我自己做。
examples.pinyin: Yàoshi nǐ yǒu kòng, jiù lái bāngmáng, fǒuzé wǒ zìjǐ zuò.
examples.translation: If you are free, come and help me; otherwise, I will do it myself.

examples.hanzi: 要是明天天晴，我们就出发，否则再等一天。
examples.pinyin: Yàoshi míngtiān tiān qíng, wǒmen jiù chūfā, fǒuzé zài děng yī tiān.
examples.translation: If the weather is good tomorrow, we will leave; otherwise, we will wait another day.

title: A necessary condition with 除非 and 才
explanation: 除非……才…… presents a necessary condition: the result can occur only if it is met. This alone does not guarantee that the condition is sufficient to produce it.

examples.hanzi: 除非你亲自去，才能弄清楚。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi nǐ qīnzì qù, cái néng nòng qīngchu.
examples.translation: Only by going in person can you clarify the situation.

examples.hanzi: 除非大家同意，计划才会改变。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi dàjiā tóngyì, jìhuà cái huì gǎibiàn.
examples.translation: The plan will change only if everyone agrees.

title: The exception that prevents an outcome
pattern: 除非 + exception，否则／不然 + outcome
explanation: 除非 introduces the exceptional condition that can prevent what follows; 否则 or 不然 describes what applies if that exception does not occur. Unlike 除非……才……, the second part is phrased as the outcome in the absence of the condition.

examples.hanzi: 除非下大雨，否则我们照常出发。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi xià dà yǔ, fǒuzé wǒmen zhàocháng chūfā.
examples.translation: Unless it rains heavily, we will leave as planned.

examples.hanzi: 除非你提醒他，不然他会忘记。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi nǐ tíxǐng tā, bùrán tā huì wàngjì.
examples.translation: Unless you remind him, he will forget.

title: Consequence with 因而
explanation: 因而 introduces a consequence derived from the preceding situation. It is common in writing and links clauses rather than introducing a noun denoting a cause on its own.

examples.hanzi: 设备出了问题，因而生产暂停了。
examples.pinyin: Shèbèi chū le wèntí, yīn'ér shēngchǎn zàntíng le.
examples.translation: The equipment developed a problem, so production was suspended.

examples.hanzi: 他准备充分，因而表现很出色。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǔnbèi chōngfèn, yīn'ér biǎoxiàn hěn chūsè.
examples.translation: He had prepared well and therefore performed excellently.

title: Concession including hypothetical conditions
explanation: 即使 concedes a condition, even a merely hypothetical or extreme one, and states that the outcome remains valid. 也 signals that this condition is not enough to change the conclusion.

examples.hanzi: 即使下雨，我们也要去。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ xià yǔ, wǒmen yě yào qù.
examples.translation: Even if it rains, we will still go.

examples.hanzi: 即使你不同意，我也会试试。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ nǐ bù tóngyì, wǒ yě huì shìshi.
examples.translation: Even if you disagree, I will try anyway.

title: Making the purpose explicit
explanation: 为的是 clarifies the goal for which the preceding action is performed. It introduces an intentional purpose, not an accidental result.

examples.hanzi: 我每天练习，为的是提高口语水平。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān liànxí, wèi de shì tígāo kǒuyǔ shuǐpíng.
examples.translation: I practice every day to improve my speaking skills.

examples.hanzi: 他提前出发，为的是避开堵车。
examples.pinyin: Tā tíqián chūfā, wèi de shì bìkāi dǔchē.
examples.translation: He left early to avoid traffic.

title: Creating the conditions for a purpose
explanation: 以便 introduces what the preceding action aims to make possible or easier. It is frequent in instructions and written language.

examples.hanzi: 请留下电话，以便我们联系您。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng liúxià diànhuà, yǐbiàn wǒmen liánxì nín.
examples.translation: Please leave a phone number so that we can contact you.

examples.hanzi: 我把资料分类，以便查找。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zīliào fēnlèi, yǐbiàn cházhǎo.
examples.translation: I sorted the materials into categories to make them easier to find.

title: Necessary dependence between two elements
explanation: This structure states that without A, B does not exist or cannot occur. It expresses strong dependence, including in reflections and expressions of gratitude, not a simple temporal sequence.

examples.hanzi: 没有水，就没有生命。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu shuǐ, jiù méiyǒu shēngmìng.
examples.translation: Without water, there is no life.

examples.hanzi: 没有你的帮助，就没有今天的成绩。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu nǐ de bāngzhù, jiù méiyǒu jīntiān de chéngjì.
examples.translation: Without your help, I would not have achieved what I have today.

title: Not even at a greater degree
explanation: 再 presents a further or extreme degree, while 也 states that the conclusion does not change. Here 再 does not simply mean again; the second part often expresses a limit or a firm decision.

examples.hanzi: 再忙也要吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Zài máng yě yào chīfàn.
examples.translation: No matter how busy you are, you must eat.

examples.hanzi: 路再远，我也要去。
examples.pinyin: Lù zài yuǎn, wǒ yě yào qù.
examples.translation: No matter how far away it is, I still want to go.

title: Logical relationships on two levels
pattern: simple clause + complex sentence；complex sentence + simple clause
explanation: A sentence can combine a simple clause with a unit already containing two linked clauses. Distinguish the main relationship, such as contrast or cause, from the internal relationship, such as a condition or concession.

examples.hanzi: 我很想去，但是如果下雨，我就留在家里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎng qù, dànshì rúguǒ xià yǔ, wǒ jiù liú zài jiā lǐ.
examples.translation: I would really like to go, but if it rains, I will stay home.

examples.hanzi: 虽然很累，但是工作还没完成，所以他没有休息。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì gōngzuò hái méi wánchéng, suǒyǐ tā méiyǒu xiūxi.
examples.translation: Although he was tired, the work was not finished, so he did not rest.

title: Definitive negation with 再也
pattern: 再也不 + verb；再也没 + verb
explanation: 再也不 expresses a negative decision or prediction from that point onward. 再也没 reports that an event never happened again after a past point; 也 strengthens the negation.

examples.hanzi: 我再也不迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yě bù chídào le.
examples.translation: I will never be late again.

examples.hanzi: 毕业以后，我再也没见过他。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè yǐhòu, wǒ zài yě méi jiàn guo tā.
examples.translation: After graduation, I never saw him again.

title: Colloquial emphasis with 可
explanation: 可 strengthens an assertion, warning, or contrast with what the listener might think. Here it does not indicate possibility and is not equivalent to 可以.

examples.hanzi: 这件事可不能忘。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì kě bù néng wàng.
examples.translation: You really must not forget this.

examples.hanzi: 我可没说过这句话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kě méi shuō guo zhè jù huà.
examples.translation: I have absolutely never said that.

title: No attempt succeeds
pattern: 怎么 + 都／也 + 不／没 + predicate
explanation: 怎么都 and 怎么也 with negation state that no method or attempt changes the outcome. 不 can refer to present impossibility or refusal, while 没 denies the result of attempts already made.

examples.hanzi: 这扇门怎么也打不开。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shàn mén zěnme yě dǎ bu kāi.
examples.translation: This door will not open no matter what I do.

examples.hanzi: 我怎么都没找到本子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zěnme dōu méi zhǎodào běnzi.
examples.translation: I could not find the notebook no matter how hard I tried.

title: Two equally unsuitable options
explanation: This pattern presents two possible actions as equally inappropriate. It expresses awkwardness or indecision, not ordinary negation of identity with 是.

examples.hanzi: 我现在走也不是，留也不是。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài zǒu yě bù shì, liú yě bù shì.
examples.translation: Right now, neither leaving nor staying feels right.

examples.hanzi: 这件事说也不是，不说也不是。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì shuō yě bù shì, bù shuō yě bù shì.
examples.translation: Regarding this matter, neither speaking nor remaining silent is appropriate.

title: Two equally impracticable actions
explanation: Each verb is repeated around 也 and followed by 不得: neither action is permitted, bearable, or practicable. The pattern highlights a situation with no easy way out.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子骂也骂不得，打也打不得。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi mà yě mà bu de, dǎ yě dǎ bu de.
examples.translation: You can neither scold nor hit this child.

examples.hanzi: 这件旧衣服穿也穿不得，扔也扔不得。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn jiù yīfu chuān yě chuān bu de, rēng yě rēng bu de.
examples.translation: This old outfit can no longer be worn, but cannot be thrown away either.

title: The same choice despite alternatives
explanation: 它 refers back to the same choice or situation, which remains unchanged even when opposite outcomes or evaluations are considered. The expression insists on accepting it or having no real alternatives; it does not mean both actions are wrong.

examples.hanzi: 好是它，坏也是它，我已经选了。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo shì tā, huài yě shì tā, wǒ yǐjīng xuǎn le.
examples.translation: Whether it is good or bad, this is the choice, and I have already made it.

examples.hanzi: 等半小时是它，等一小时也是它，今天只有这班车。
examples.pinyin: Děng bàn xiǎoshí shì tā, děng yī xiǎoshí yě shì tā, jīntiān zhǐ yǒu zhè bān chē.
examples.translation: Whether we wait half an hour or an hour, we have to take this service: it is the only one today.

title: We would be doing it anyway
explanation: Repeating the verb with 着 presents a state as otherwise unused time. The pattern justifies an alternative suggestion: since we are waiting, sitting, or doing nothing anyway, we might as well do something else.

examples.hanzi: 闲着也是闲着，不如帮我做饭。
examples.pinyin: Xián zhe yě shì xián zhe, bùrú bāng wǒ zuò fàn.
examples.translation: Since you have nothing to do, you might as well help me cook.

examples.hanzi: 等着也是等着，我们说说话吧。
examples.pinyin: Děng zhe yě shì děng zhe, wǒmen shuō shuo huà ba.
examples.translation: Since we have to wait anyway, let us have a chat.

title: Keeping two matters separate
explanation: Repetition with 归 separates areas that should not be confused, such as friendship and business. It can also acknowledge an activity or fact without allowing it to change the rest of the situation.

examples.hanzi: 朋友归朋友，生意归生意。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou guī péngyou, shēngyi guī shēngyi.
examples.translation: Friendship is one thing; business is another.

examples.hanzi: 吵归吵，闹归闹，我们还是一家人。
examples.pinyin: Chǎo guī chǎo, nào guī nào, wǒmen háishi yī jiā rén.
examples.translation: We may argue and make a fuss, but we are still a family.

title: However you look at it
explanation: 不管怎样说 introduces a conclusion the speaker considers valid despite different interpretations or arguments. It can also close a discussion by returning to the essential point.

examples.hanzi: 不管怎样说，你都应该说对不起。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn zěnyàng shuō, nǐ dōu yīnggāi shuō duìbuqǐ.
examples.translation: However you look at it, you should apologize.

examples.hanzi: 不管怎样说，问题已经解决了。
examples.pinyin: Bùguǎn zěnyàng shuō, wèntí yǐjīng jiějué le.
examples.translation: In any case, the problem has been solved.

title: Reacting to someone’s behavior
pattern: 看你 + predicate + 的；瞧他 + predicate + 的
explanation: This form draws attention to an obvious behavior or state with an exclamatory tone. It can express reproach, irony, or affectionate involvement; the judgment depends on the predicate and context.

examples.hanzi: 看你急的，车还没来呢。
examples.pinyin: Kàn nǐ jí de, chē hái méi lái ne.
examples.translation: Look how worked up you are; the bus has not arrived yet.

examples.hanzi: 瞧他高兴的，嘴都合不上了。
examples.pinyin: Qiáo tā gāoxìng de, zuǐ dōu hé bu shàng le.
examples.translation: Look how happy he is; he cannot stop smiling.

title: Recognizing unexpected ability
pattern: 真有 + 你／他／她 + 的
explanation: 真有你的 and the variants with 他 or 她 express admiration for skill, ingenuity, or a remarkable achievement. Context can make them ironic, but they are not expressions of literal possession.

examples.hanzi: 这么快就修好了，真有你的。
examples.pinyin: Zhème kuài jiù xiū hǎo le, zhēn yǒu nǐ de.
examples.translation: You fixed it so quickly; you really are capable.

examples.hanzi: 她连这道难题都解开了，真有她的。
examples.pinyin: Tā lián zhè dào nántí dōu jiěkāi le, zhēn yǒu tā de.
examples.translation: She solved even this difficult problem; she is really good.

title: Interrupting or challenging an action
explanation: X什么X is a colloquial retort challenging the appropriateness of an action: why do it, or stop doing it. It is not a request for information about an object.

examples.hanzi: 笑什么笑，快来帮忙。
examples.pinyin: Xiào shénme xiào, kuài lái bāngmáng.
examples.translation: What are you laughing at? Come and help right now.

examples.hanzi: 急什么急，还有时间。
examples.pinyin: Jí shénme jí, hái yǒu shíjiān.
examples.translation: Why the rush? There is still time.

title: Rejecting a distinction or concern
pattern: 什么 + X + 不 + X +（的）
explanation: This pattern dismisses the relevance of a distinction such as expensive or not expensive, or a concern mentioned by the listener. It often reassures or rejects formalities rather than asking whether X is true.

examples.hanzi: 什么麻烦不麻烦的，你尽管说。
examples.pinyin: Shénme máfan bù máfan de, nǐ jǐnguǎn shuō.
examples.translation: Do not worry about bothering me; go ahead and tell me.

examples.hanzi: 什么贵不贵的，喜欢就买。
examples.pinyin: Shénme guì bù guì de, xǐhuan jiù mǎi.
examples.translation: Never mind whether it is expensive; if you like it, buy it.

title: Referring back in discourse
explanation: A personal pronoun refers back to a person already introduced; a demonstrative can refer back to an object, an event, or an entire situation. Both types can alternate in the same passage, provided each referent remains clear.

examples.hanzi: 我认识一位画家。她住在附近。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ rènshi yī wèi huàjiā. Tā zhù zài fùjìn.
examples.translation: I know a painter. She lives nearby.

examples.hanzi: 昨天停电了。这让大家很不方便。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān tíng diàn le. Zhè ràng dàjiā hěn bù fāngbiàn.
examples.translation: The power went out yesterday. This caused everyone a lot of inconvenience.

examples.hanzi: 小王买了一辆车。他每天开这辆车上班。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo Wáng mǎi le yī liàng chē. Tā měitiān kāi zhè liàng chē shàng bān.
examples.translation: Xiao Wang bought a car. He uses it to go to work every day.

title: Omitting what is already clear
explanation: In linked clauses, a subject can be omitted when it has already been identified and remains unchanged. An object recoverable from context can also be omitted; the omission must not create ambiguity about who acts or what receives the action.

examples.hanzi: 姐姐回到家，放下包就去做饭。
examples.pinyin: Jiějie huí dào jiā, fàngxià bāo jiù qù zuò fàn.
examples.translation: My older sister came home, put down her bag, and started cooking.

examples.hanzi: 这本书很好看，我已经看过了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn hǎokàn, wǒ yǐjīng kàn guo le.
examples.translation: This book is very good; I have already read it.
